prompt: Where does the lesson keep a 5 MB PDF of course notes?

choices.text: In a blob column beside the sessions, so one backup and one transaction cover both
choices.why: That is the tempting design the section takes apart: the database grew to 5136 KB.

choices.text: In shared_prefs/, encoded as base64
choices.why: Preferences are for small settings and are read whole.

choices.text: On disk, with a row holding its path, size and hash
choices.why: Right. The database stayed at 12 KB.

choices.text: In the HTTP cache
choices.why: The cache may vanish; lesson 17 keeps only copies there.

prompt: Which problems does the lesson give for large blobs inside SQLite? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: a `select *` reads megabytes to show a title
choices.why: Reading the row reads the chain of pages.

choices.text: the file does not shrink until a VACUUM
choices.why: Freed pages are reused, not returned.

choices.text: a backup rule cannot exclude one row
choices.why: Rules name files, not rows.

choices.text: SQLite refuses values over 1 MB
choices.why: It stored 5 MB in the lesson's run.

prompt: Why is the attachment's file named after the SHA-256 of its contents?

choices.text: Equal contents share one file, checkable later
choices.why: Right. Hashing it again tells whether the file still matches its row.

choices.text: To hide what it is from other apps
choices.why: Other apps cannot read the sandbox anyway.

choices.text: Because file systems on phones refuse names with spaces in them
choices.why: They accept spaces; that is not the reason.

choices.text: So the backup skips it
choices.why: A name decides nothing about backup; the folder does.

prompt: A server answers a `Range: bytes=1048576-` request with only that part. Which status does it send?

choices.text: 200 OK, the whole file again
choices.why: 200 is the whole file, as on the first request.

choices.text: 304 Not Modified
choices.why: 304 has no body; it says the copy is current.

choices.text: 416 Range Not Satisfiable
choices.why: That is for a range outside the file.

choices.text: 206 Partial Content
choices.why: Right, with a Content-Range saying which part.

prompt: The notes are edited on the server between the two requests. Without `If-Range`, what does the resumed download produce?

choices.text: The new file whole, because a 206 always carries the latest version
choices.why: A 206 carries the range asked for, of whatever the file is now.

choices.text: A file made of two versions
choices.why: Right. The old first megabyte meets the new rest, and no hash will match.

choices.text: An error from the server refusing the range
choices.why: Nothing tells the server to refuse; that is If-Range's job.

choices.text: The old file whole, read from the part
choices.why: Only a third of it was there.

prompt: In the lesson's run, at which byte did the second request resume?
Why does download.ts give up after half a second of silence instead of waiting for the connection to close?

choices.text: Node closes every connection after 0.5 s
choices.why: Node keeps a connection open; the timeout is the app's.

choices.text: A dead connection on a phone goes quiet rather than closing
choices.why: Right. Half a second suits a capture; a real app waits tens of seconds.

choices.text: The server asks it to in a header
choices.why: No header asks it.

choices.text: To keep the file small
choices.why: It wants the whole file; it just keeps what arrived.

prompt: Put save.ts's steps in the order the lesson requires.
items: ask statfs whether there is room
rename it to its real name

prompt: What does `/dev/full` stand in for in the lesson's run?

choices.text: A file the planner may delete when it is done
choices.why: It is a device and not the planner's, which is why save.ts checks isFile.

choices.text: The backup quota of Android
choices.why: That was lesson 1's 25 MB, a different limit.

choices.text: A slow network
choices.why: It has nothing to do with the network.

choices.text: A full disk
choices.why: Right: a disk that runs out on the first write. Every write to it fails with ENOSPC.

prompt: A planner inserts the row, then downloads the file, and the disk fills at 20 of 30 MB. What does the person meet on the plane?

choices.text: Notes the app says are there, which fail to open
choices.why: Right. The row came before the whole file.

choices.text: A message asking to free space, shown before the download
choices.why: That is what asking statfs first would have given.

choices.text: Nothing missing: the database rolls the row back when the write fails
choices.why: The row was committed before the file was written; nothing ties them.

choices.text: The full 30 MB, since the system makes room
choices.why: Without allocateBytes, nothing was reserved.

prompt: The error a write returns on Linux and Android when the disk is full is called ___.
Match each platform to how it reports space the app may use.
The sweep finds a file in attachments/ that no row names. What does it do?

choices.text: Uploads it to the server in case it matters
choices.why: Nothing says what it is; the sweep does not guess.

choices.text: Adds a row for it, guessing the name from the hash
choices.why: A hash cannot give back the name or what it belonged to.

choices.text: Deletes it
choices.why: Right. Nothing can reach it, so it is only disk used.

choices.text: Moves it to cache/
choices.why: It would still be a file nothing reaches.

prompt: Why does sweep.ts skip files ending in `.part`?

choices.text: They are downloads in progress, not orphans
choices.why: Right. Deleting one throws away what the resume would use.

choices.text: The system deletes them on its own at the next restart of the phone
choices.why: attachments/ is not a folder the system clears.

choices.text: They are too small to matter
choices.why: A part can be most of a large file.

choices.text: Their rows are kept in a different table
choices.why: A part has no row at all, by design.

prompt: A photo the person attached to a session is missing from the disk. Should the sweep remove its row as it did for notes.pdf?

choices.text: Yes: a row with no file is an orphan
choices.why: For a downloaded copy, yes; this one cannot be downloaded again.

choices.text: Yes, and the server sends the photo back
choices.why: Unless it was uploaded, the server never had it.

choices.text: No: it is a loss to report, not a row to tidy
choices.why: Right. Only a copy the server has can be fetched again on the next open.

choices.text: No: rows are never removed
choices.why: The sweep removed notes.pdf's row, on purpose.

prompt: Why is renaming the part file the moment a download counts as complete?

choices.text: Renaming copies the bytes, checking each one
choices.why: A rename within a folder moves no bytes.

choices.text: It is atomic: before it there is no notes.pdf, after it a whole one
choices.why: Right. No reader can see a half file under the real name.

choices.text: It frees the space the part took
choices.why: The same blocks stay; only the name changes.

choices.text: The server is told of it
choices.why: The server knows nothing of the rename.

prompt: After the lesson's run, which of these were true at the end? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: guitar-tabs.pdf had been deleted from the disk
choices.why: It was an orphan file.

choices.text: spanish-verbs.pdf still had its row and its file
choices.why: The sweep left it alone.

choices.text: notes.pdf had been downloaded again by the sweep
choices.why: The sweep removed the row; the next open downloads it.

choices.text: the table held two rows
choices.why: It held one: sweep done, 1 attachments.

prompt: save.ts asks statfs for twice the file's size. What is the second half for?

choices.text: A second copy kept as a backup
choices.why: No second copy is made.

choices.text: The part and the final file, both kept
choices.why: A rename leaves one file, not two.

choices.text: The compressed copy
choices.why: Nothing is compressed.

choices.text: Room for the database's writes and the rest of the phone
choices.why: Right. Filling the disk to the last byte breaks everything else.
